newsitem.title: USA: API head says recent heat oil price surge overdone.
newsitem.headline: API head says recent heat oil price surge overdone.

text.p: The head of the American Petroleum Institute (API) said Thursday that the surge in heating oil prices in recent months was overdone.

Charles DiBona, president of the API, said at a briefing in New York that the response in recent weeks by the oil industry to government and media concern over low stocks showed that it could quickly react to any percieved shortage in inventories.
"When a problem occurred the industry has shown incredible adaptability," said DiBona. "The most important source of supply -- day-to-day refinery production -- has been reaching record levels."

Indeed, the API was surprised at the strength of the inventory build in the past few weeks and the extent that industry was able to switch its output to heating oil and diesel production from gasoline.

"After producing 3.6 million barrels a day for over two weeks our statistics head didn't believe we were going to see it maintain that level. But we see in the third week now it was over 3.8 million barrels," he said.

Heating oil prices ran up 50 pct from the summer lows to hit a peak on the New York Mercantile Exchange of 76.75 cents a gallon earlier this month, the highest level since the middle of the Gulf War in January, 1991.
Prices have since collapsed by 14 pct, dipping below 66 cents a gallon on Thursday, as refiners rushed to pump out product.
